$comment: Windows (tools/content/kit/campus.mjs; docs/map-briefs/st_johns, step 9): stained glass of our own colours drawn on both faces of the wall it is set in (the wall is solid behind it: a window to look at, not through). Nothing glows or blinks.

notes.1: First version (St. John's step 9, photos 11 and 21): a tall pointed window 2.2 x 6 m in a stone surround, two lights under a round eye, filled with small panes of our own colours between dark leading; drawn on both faces of the wall it is set in (depth 0.58: a 0.5 m wall and a hair each side), the wall solid behind it. Steady colours, nothing glows. Collides as nothing. Variants: blue (deep blues with flecks of gold, red and green), amber (golds and reds).

First version (St. John's step 9, photo 11: the small round window high in the end wall over the altar): a wheel 3.2 m across in a stone ring, twelve spokes from a round centre, small panes of our own colours; drawn on both faces of its wall, the wall solid behind. Collides as nothing.

First version (St. John's step 8b; the owner's photo: a band of wide cream-framed windows of several panes tight under the eave, about a third of the upper storey's height, nearly touching one another): a window 3 m wide and 1.3 m high drawn on both faces of the 0.5 m wall it is set in: a thick cream frame, three lights of four panes each. A window to look at, not through (the wall is solid). Collides as nothing.
notes.2: Variant `open` (St. John's Memorial Hall pass, owner 2026-11-23: windows of breakable glass, clear, to see and shoot through): the frame and mullions alone round a real opening in the wall, lined through its depth, no panes of its own; a glass pane (a breakable glass block) fills the opening, and once it is shot the window is open.
notes.3: Variant `open`: the frame's four bars are boxes through the wall's depth (owner, 2026-11-24, St. John's: a slit of light at a window's head and up its jambs). The lining stood 2 cm inside the wall's cut and the outer bar was drawn facing out only, so the channel between them showed the sky from the room; the bars now close it, the lining their inner faces.

notes.1: First version (St. John's step 8b; the owner's photo: square dark windows of several panes in thick pale smooth stone surrounds in the fieldstone storey): a window 1.5 m square drawn on both faces of the 0.5 m wall it is set in: a thick pale stone surround and sill, two lights of six dark leaded panes each. A window to look at, not through. Collides as nothing.
notes.2: Variant `open` (St. John's Memorial Hall pass, owner 2026-11-23: windows of breakable glass, clear, to see and shoot through): the frame and mullions alone round a real opening in the wall, lined through its depth, no panes of its own; a glass pane (a breakable glass block) fills the opening, and once it is shot the window is open.
notes.3: Variant `open`: the frame's four bars are boxes through the wall's depth (owner, 2026-11-24, St. John's: a slit of light at a window's head and up its jambs). The lining stood 2 cm inside the wall's cut and the outer bar was drawn facing out only, so the channel between them showed the sky from the room; the bars now close it, the lining their inner faces.
